newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Alcatel shares jump despite Thomson.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Alcatel shares jump despite Thomson.

text.p: Shares in French industrial giant Alcatel Alsthom jumped on the Paris stock exchange on Wednesday after the French government snubbed its bid for Thomson SA.
But dealers said the 2.4 percent rise to 455.70 francs was due to short covering and followed a fall of over two percent on Tuesday on the back of rumours Alcatel had not lost but won.
On balance, dealers and analysts said the government decision removed uncertainty about Alcatel's financial future but at the same time clipped its industrial ambitions.
The French government said on Wednesday it preferred a bid by Lagardere, which owns defence company Matra, and planned to sell it the debt-laden state-owned Thomson for a symbolic franc.
French brokers Cheuvreux de Virieu and CCF Elysees Bourse as well as American broker Morgan Stanley upgraded their recommendations for Alcatel and advised investors to buy.
"I think it is a good decision. For Lagardere, for Alcatel, but not for the taxpayer," one financial analyst said.

Another said Alcatel would have become too dispersed a conglomerate if it had won. "There is now not going to be a dispersion of energy. The group can continue its restructuring and bring back some order is its activities, in particular in telecoms," he said.
In a statement, Alcatel "noted" the government decision and hoped it would preserve French and European defence interests.
Several investors had been worried about the impact on Alcatel's current recovery programme, designed to pull it back into profit after last year's heavy loss from restructuring.
One broking firm said it had a target of 500 to 520 francs a share for Alcatel, compared a high for the year so far of 500 francs and a 1996 low of 368 francs.
But behind the share recovery, analysts highlighted that the planned sale of Thomson to Lagardere had dealt a blow to the industrial ambitions of Alcatel chairman Serge Tchuruk.
"It was the last major opportunity for growth in France and in Europe," one analyst said, adding Wednesday's share buying came mostly from investors who had previously sold short.
Tchuruk, hired last year, wanted to turn Alcatel into a telecommunications, defence electronics and engineering giant.
After reshaping Alcatel, putting a new organisational structure in place and cutting 30,000 jobs, Tchuruk sought to vault the ailing group to the top ranks globally.

Tchuruk took hefty charges last year which plunged Alcatel into a 25.6 billion franc ($4.91 billion) loss -- the biggest in French corporate history. Alcatel hopes to break even this year and make good profits from 1998.
To boost its telecoms activities, its core business, Alcatel concluded technology pacts with Sharp and Motorola.

Tchuruk had sought to turn Thomson's defence unit Thomson-CSF into the world's number two defence company in a deal which could involve a British group or Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace GmbH (DASA). He also aimed to find an Asian partner for the Thomson Multimedia business.
On another front, analysts noted his plans to acquire state nuclear engineering company Framatome through its GEC Alsthom venture with Britain's GEC Plc seem to be hitting opposition.
On August 30, the government allowed GEC-Alsthom to start negotations to merge with state-controlled Framatome in which Alcatel holds 44 percent stake.
Tchuruk said Alcatel, which would initially obtain a bigger say in the GEC Alsthom Framatome venture than GEC, aimed to put part of the engineering group on the market in a few years.
But while the talks have not been concluded, some French parliamentarians are expressing dismay over what they call a "secret pact" and are demanding more transparency in the talks.
($1=5.210 French Franc)
